properties.name: READ storyflow's extraction on ajs77: the "schema up front" analogy holds in the ORDER of passes and the gating, and fails in the one place Anthony's sentence put it — defining the terms
properties.statement:
READ 2026-09-14 on ajs77, at Anthony's direction. Source: storyflow/services/generation_plus/src/modules/extraction/ (multi_pass_orchestrator.py, passes/_common.py, passes/discovery.py, passes/interpersonal_relationships.py, schema_driven.py, dimension_vocabulary.py, graph_informed_*.py), dev_storyflow/docs/architecture/multi_pass_extraction_lessons.md (715 lines, "last refined 2026-05-13", every claim cited to a commit), the archived design note project_extraction_multi_pass.md, and dev_storyflow's own reflow2 export (3,177 nodes). Code and lessons doc read directly, not summarised from a note.

═══ WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS ═══

Not two passes — a THREE-PHASE fan-out of 17 focused passes, replacing one ~5,100-word monolithic prompt (2026-05-11→13):
  Phase 1 (parallel): five always-run entity passes + ONE discovery classifier, all reading prose only.
  Phase 2 (parallel): entity passes for objects/concepts/groups, GATED by Phase-1 discovery flags.
  Phase 3 (parallel): typed-edge passes, each CONDITIONED on the rosters Phases 1–2 produced ("CHARACTERS PRESENT: A, B, C").
Every pass has its own output schema (Pydantic per pass). Cost recorded in their design: ~17 LLM calls per fragment (con:extraction_calls_per_fragment). Made affordable by a byte-deterministic shared prefix so the model's implicit prompt cache hits across passes — and that invariant is called "the load-bearing surface".

═══ ⭐ THE FOUR THINGS THAT TRANSFER, AND ONE THAT DOES NOT ═══

(1) THE MONOLITH WAS BLIND TO WHOLE FAMILIES. Measured on the same prose: hierarchy edges 0/10 under the monolith, 10/10 per-axis; interpersonal relationships 40%→100%; causal chains 30%→100%; the orchestrator produced "2× richer graphs". The lesson is not "more passes" — it is that ONE prompt asked for everything systematically under-extracts some kinds. reflow2's capture-intent is a monolith of exactly that shape: one skill, one pass, every node type at once. Whether it is blind to a family (Interfaces? Flows? Constraints?) is MEASURABLE on reflow2's own design and has not been measured.

(2) ⭐⭐ THE ORTHOGONAL-AXIS PRINCIPLE, AND ITS SHARP LIMIT — the finding that bears directly on Anthony's sentence. Lesson #1: "define a tuple of mutually-exclusive types and let the LLM pick one. Do NOT define what each type means — for real-world concepts the LLM has strong priors. Per-type definitions are noise that dilutes the orthogonal list." 11 relationship types, no definitions: 100% where the monolith with definitions hit 40%. Lesson #2: "the principle has a sharp limit when the axis names INVENTED DOMAIN TERMS the LLM has no prior on." interiority_mode actual/perceived/mixed regressed to 0/5 because the model's prior on "perceived" was wrong for the domain — fixed with an ~80-word VERB-TEST DISCRIMINATOR: entity ACTS → actual; entity is FELT/DESCRIBED → perceived. So: a schema "with all the SE terms defined up front" is the WRONG shape for the terms a model already knows, and the RIGHT shape — as a discriminating test, not a definition — for the terms whose lay meaning collides with the SE meaning. Alex's "query" is the second kind: the model's prior on the word is strong and points AWAY from the SE routing. The transferable object is a verb test per SE axis — does it ACT (Capability), does it PROMISE (Requirement), is it WHERE TWO THINGS MEET (Interface), is it ORDERED (Flow) — not a glossary.

(3) ⭐ THE DISCOVERY CLASSIFIER IS HOW THEY ANSWERED "CAN THE MODEL TELL WHAT'S THERE?" — the question dec:idea-extraction-is-two-pass… and dec:idea-the-interviews-answers… both said nothing had demonstrated. They did NOT ask the model to introspect on its own ambiguity. They ask seven narrow binary presence questions at temperature 0 with ANCHOR-REQUIRED gating: "return true ONLY when you can point to a concrete in-prose instance." The first draft ("bias toward recall, return true when uncertain") collapsed to constant-true — foreshadowing fired on café banter. So the shape that works is a gate that demands a pointer to evidence, and it gates whether the expensive pass RUNS at all. That is the mechanism reflow2's option (d) needs and did not have.

(4) THE GRAPH-INFORMED RESOLUTION PASS IS THE PER-PROJECT INHERITED REFERENCE, ALREADY BUILT OVER THERE. Pass 2 feeds back "KNOWN CHARACTERS (ranked by importance — use these to resolve unnamed references, nicknames, abbreviations)", ranked by mention count or PageRank past 50. The glossary IS the graph, ranked, re-injected at capture. reflow2 has the pieces (search_design, record_alias) and does not feed them back at capture; dec:idea-search-expands-with-the-projects-own-domain-vocabulary is the open question on that.

(5) WHAT DOES NOT TRANSFER: schema_driven.py generates prompt supplements FROM the graph schema YAML (add a domain YAML → the prompt includes it, no code). That is "SE terms defined up front" as DATA the prompt is built from — but their own constraint says adding one node type is 12 coordinated edits across 3 services, 4 of which fail SILENTLY (con:adding_one_node_type_costs_twelve_coordinated_edits…). reflow2's vocabulary is fixed and served; the generation-from-schema idea buys nothing here.

═══ ONE MORE MEASUREMENT WORTH CARRYING ═══
dimension_vocabulary.py: with a prompt that said "use these or other narratively-natural labels", the store held 25–26 distinct dimension keys against ten declared, and 16 of 19 free inventions were HOLLOW nodes (no score, no evidence). Fix: fold two aliases, drop-and-COUNT the rest at the write boundary. That is evidence for a fixed label set — enforced at validation, not by defining terms in the prompt — and it is the agent-facing half of dec:idea-the-user-declares-an-se-unit… measured on someone else's data.

═══ BOUNDS ═══
One project, one domain (narrative prose), one model family; the lessons doc is four months old and self-describes as living. reflow2's inputs are short design statements, not 4 KB prose fragments, so the caching economics do not carry. Nothing here says reflow2 SHOULD split its capture — only that whether its monolith is blind to a family is now a cheap, well-defined measurement instead of a guess.
